en.meaning: People who want quick success worship radiant beings, because results from action come quickly in the human world.

hi.meaning: फल की कामना करने वाले मनुष्य देवताओं की उपासना करते हैं क्योंकि मनुष्य लोक में कर्म से उत्पन्न होने वाली सिद्धि जल्दी मिल जाती है।

en.intro: Krishna carries on from his teaching that all paths lead to Him, and now He shows why people still look elsewhere for quick fixes.
en.body: People who want quick success worship radiant beings, because results from action come quickly in the human world. The word kanksantah, desiring, reveals the restless pull of the mind. People do not worship the devas because they are wise; they do so because they want fast results, and in the human world action can indeed produce quick fruit. Krishna now turns to the very origin of these divisions and the social orders that bind them together.

issues: borrowed: "अब कृष्ण उन विभाजनों के उद्गम की ओर मुड़ते हैं जो समाज को बाँधते हैं।" (The Hindi 'next' (NEXT) for verse 12 incorrectly presents the content of verse 13 (the origin of the four social orders) as if it were part of verse 12's transition. This borrows the next verse's content into the current verse's 'next' field.)

wrong_fact: "संजय, अब तुम मेरे इस ज्ञान और कर्म के रहस्य को और विस्तार से समझो।" (The notice in the Hindi script attributes this line to Krishna speaking to 'Sanjaya'. However, Sanjaya is the narrator of the Mahabharata to Dhritarashtra, not a participant in the battlefield dialogue. In the context of the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna is speaking to Arjuna. This is a factual error regarding the listener/speaker relation.)

wrong_fact: "संजय, अब तुम मेरे इस ज्ञान और कर्म के रहस्य को और विस्तार से समझो।" (The Hindi 'next' misattributes the speaker as Sanjaya, who is the narrator/listener in the Mahabharata, not the speaker of this verse (Krishna).)
